faq_heading: Selling in Langley: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from the City of Langley's notice for Bylaw 3289, a development-industry summary of the Township of Langley's 2024 change (the Township's own pages could not be read automatically) and the Province's short-term rental page, read 2026-11-01. The Township's unit rules and both Langleys' short-term rental rules are not confirmed and are marked as such. Nothing here states a commission, fee or marketing package; those are for Jared to supply. The older page /sell-my-house-fast-in-langley-bc.html stays as it is.

Langley is two governments. The Township of Langley covers Willoughby, Walnut Grove, Murrayville, Brookswood, Aldergrove and the rural land. The City of Langley is the small downtown core. Each has its own zoning bylaw, so a seller needs to know which one holds the title.

This page gives the benchmark prices for Langley, what each government has done about the 2024 housing rules and what I need to price your home. If you need to sell on a short timeline, my page on selling fast in Langley covers the strategy.
Selling fast in Langley
Langley home prices, September 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical Langley home was $941,800 in September 2026, down 6.2% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,471,100 (down 6.7% over the year), townhouses $802,600 (down 4.4%) and apartments $525,900 (down 9.2%).

blocks.text: City of Langley: Plex-Homes on RS1 and RS2 lots

The City of Langley added a new use called a Plex-Home by Bylaw 3284 on June 17, 2024. It permits 4 to 6 units on RS1 and RS2 lots. A second bylaw, 3289 (Zoning Bylaw Amendment No. 209), set the parking for it. The City gave notice of first and second readings for July 8, 2024, and said no public hearing would be held under section 464(4) of the Local Government Act. The notice does not say whether 3289 was adopted, so I have not stated that it was.

blocks.text: Township of Langley: what I can and cannot say

A development-industry summary dated December 2, 2024 reports that Council gave first, second and third reading to the Township's zoning amendments on June 10, 2024, deferred final adoption, and adopted them on November 18. It also says a Form and Character development permit area for these homes was nearing finalization and that the Township was updating its water and sewer master plans, expected by the end of 2025, with new connections for these homes deferred until that review is complete.

The Township's own report to Council could not be read by my tools, so I have not stated the number of units per lot or the lot-size rules. Do not assume your lot qualifies for four units because a neighbouring city allows it. Send me the address and I will confirm the zone, the lot size and whether sewer and water are on the street.
Short-term rentals
I have not confirmed a short-term rental rule for either the Township or the City of Langley, so I am not stating one here.

The Province's rule sits on top of anything Langley requires. The Province says the principal residence requirement applies in municipalities with a population of 10,000 or more. A short-term rental can only be the host's usual home, "where they make their home day-to-day," plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit on the same property. A bed and breakfast is allowed only if the owner lives on the property.

Any rental for fewer than 90 consecutive days must also be registered with the Province, one registration number per unit. The Province lists the fee as $100 a year for a host's principal residence and $450 a year for a secondary unit such as a suite or cottage, and compliance with local bylaws is a condition of registration.

faq.a: No. The Township of Langley and the City of Langley are separate governments with separate zoning bylaws. The Township is much larger; the City is the compact downtown core.

faq.q: What did the City of Langley do about the 2024 housing rules?
faq.a: By Bylaw 3284 on June 17, 2024, the City added a Plex-Home use that permits 4 to 6 units on RS1 and RS2 lots. Bylaw 3289 sets the parking for it; the City's notice gave first and second readings for July 8, 2024 and did not state an adoption.

faq.q: How much parking does a City of Langley Plex-Home need?
faq.a: Under Bylaw 3289 as noticed, at least 1.5 spaces for units over 90 m² and at least 1 space for units of 90 m² or less, with none required within 400 m of a frequent bus stop.

faq.q: Has the Township of Langley adopted its housing rules?
faq.a: A development-industry summary reports that Council adopted the zoning amendments on November 18, 2024, after readings on June 10, 2024. I could not read the Township's own report, so I have not stated its unit and lot-size rules.

faq.q: Can a buyer run an Airbnb in a Langley house?
faq.a: I have not confirmed a rule for either Langley. The Province requires a short-term rental in a municipality of 10,000 or more to be the host's principal residence, plus at most one suite or accessory unit, and registered with the Province.

faq.q: How current are the prices on this page?
faq.a: The benchmark prices come from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's MLS® Home Price Index for the month shown. They describe a typical home across Langley, not your house.
